findings.title: Unrelated audit log pagination changes crash with AttributeError and TypeError
findings.body:
Aside from being unrelated to the spans buffer PR, the changes in `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get` contain two runtime bugs:
1. Line 71 evaluates `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` on every request. When a non-superuser request has no associated organization member (for example, an organization-level API token or Sentry App with `org:admin` permission), `organization_context.member` is `None`, raising `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'`.
2. When `optimized_pagination=true` is passed, lines 76-83 paginate `AuditLogEntry` ordered by `"-datetime"` using `OptimizedCursorPaginator`. However, `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `datetime.datetime` instance, and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly on the field value (unlike `DateTimePaginator`), raising `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`. Likewise, `OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor` returns the raw numeric cursor value instead of a `datetime`, causing a database type error on subsequent pages.

findings.title: Negative offset slicing on Django QuerySets raises ValueError
findings.body: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (lines 877-882), when `self.enable_advanced_features and cursor.offset < 0`, `start_offset` is set to the negative `cursor.offset` and used to slice `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Contrary to the comment claiming that the Django ORM handles negative slicing automatically, Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` whenever `start < 0` or `stop < 0`, resulting in an unhandled 500 error. The same crash occurs in `BasePaginator.get_result` (line 182) and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (line 884) whenever `cursor.is_prev` is `True` and `cursor.offset < 0` (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`). Furthermore, when `cursor.is_prev` is `False` and `offset < 0`, clamping `start_offset` to `0` while passing the negative `offset` into `build_cursor` produces corrupted `next` and `prev` cursor offsets.

findings.title: Evicting spans via zpopmin leaks redirect map entries and can evict the root span
findings.body:
When `span_count > 1000`, `add-buffer.lua` evicts the spans with the lowest `end_timestamp_precise` from `set_key` using `zpopmin`, which introduces two issues:
1. Every ingested span has its `span_id -> set_span_id` mapping written to `main_redirect_key` (`span-buf:sr:{project_id:trace_id}`) at line 40, but `SpansBuffer.done_flush_segments` (`src/sentry/spans/buffer.py`, lines 478-482) only deletes `span_id`s that are present in `flushed_segment.spans`. Any span evicted by `zpopmin` is never removed from `main_redirect_key` on flush, leaking those hash entries until the 1-hour TTL expires and causing any late-arriving child of an evicted span to be redirected to the already-flushed segment.
2. `zpopmin` evicts purely by lowest `end_timestamp_precise` without protecting the segment's root/head span (`set_span_id`). If the segment span finishes earlier than 1,000 async/background child spans in the same segment, the root span itself will be evicted while `has_root_span_key` remains `"1"`.

findings.title: max_segment_spans parameter is now unused and eviction (>1000 spans) lacks test coverage
findings.body: `SpansBuffer.__init__` still accepts `max_segment_spans: int = 1001` and stores `self.max_segment_spans` (lines 150 and 158), but its only usage in `_load_segment_data` was removed and replaced with a hardcoded `1000` limit in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` (line 62). `max_segment_spans` should either be passed to `add-buffer.lua` as an argument or removed from `SpansBuffer.__init__`, and `tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py` should include a test covering segments with more than 1,000 spans.
